title: Conduct treatment processes for health and nuisance pests

lessons.title: Rodent treatment in practice
lessons.html:
Setting up a rodent programme

Rodent control on a farm, silo complex, food factory or residence follows a practical sequence: inspect, reduce food and harbourage, proof, then trap or bait, and monitor.

Placing bait stations

  1. Use tamper-resistant bait stations, secured to the ground or a wall so they cannot be moved or opened by children, pets or livestock.
  2. Place stations along runways, next to walls and near burrows, at spacings guided by the label and your company standard.
  3. Use registered rodenticide blocks secured on rods inside the station so bait cannot be dragged out.
  4. Number each station and mark it on the site plan.
  5. Label stations with a warning, the product name and the company contact.

Inside food areas

Inside food production and storage areas, use traps (snap traps in tunnels, multi-catch traps or glue boards where permitted) rather than poison, unless the client's food safety system and the label allow otherwise. Check traps frequently and remove catches promptly.

Servicing

  • Inspect each station: bait taken, droppings, damage, non-target activity.
  • Replace mouldy or eaten bait; record consumption for each station.
  • Search for and remove carcasses wearing gloves; bag them and dispose of them as your procedure requires.
  • Report proofing and hygiene issues to the client.

Safety

Wear gloves when handling bait and carcasses. Wash hands after each job. If a person or pet may have eaten bait, get medical or veterinary help immediately with the product label. Do not induce vomiting unless a doctor or the label instructs it.

lessons.title: Treating crawling and flying insects
lessons.html:
Cockroaches

  1. Inspect at night or with a flushing agent where permitted to find harbourages: behind and under stoves, fridges, dishwashers, inside motor housings, cracks in walls and cupboards.
  2. Place sticky monitors to confirm hot spots.
  3. Ask the client to improve cleaning, fix leaks and reduce clutter.
  4. Apply gel bait in small dots into cracks and crevices close to harbourages, at the label rate, away from surfaces that are cleaned often.
  5. Use insect growth regulators where registered.
  6. Use residual sprays only where needed and as labelled, never over gel bait.
  7. Return within the planned interval to check monitors and re-bait.

Flies

  • Find and eliminate breeding sites: refuse bins, manure heaps, spilled feed and grain, blocked drains.
  • Fit or recommend screens and strip curtains.
  • Install insect light traps with catch trays in food areas, away from food lines and not visible from outside, and service them by replacing trays and tubes on schedule.
  • Apply registered baits or residual treatments to resting surfaces where justified.

Mosquitoes

Remove or treat standing water: empty containers, clean gutters, cover water tanks, and use registered larvicides where water cannot be removed. Adult control indoors may use registered residual products as the label allows.

Bed bugs and fleas

Inspect beds, furniture and skirtings. Ask the client to launder bedding hot, vacuum thoroughly and declutter. Apply registered products to harbourages as labelled, never on mattress sleeping surfaces unless the label allows it. For fleas, the owner must treat pets with veterinary products at the same time. Follow up because eggs may survive.

lessons.title: Bird management and completing the service
lessons.html:
Pest birds

Feral pigeons, sparrows and mynas roost on silo structures, warehouse beams and loading bays, fouling product and creating slip hazards. Control is mainly by exclusion:

  • Install netting to close off roof voids and loading bay beams.
  • Fit spikes, wires or sloped covers on ledges.
  • Close holes in walls and eaves.
  • Remove nests and droppings while wearing gloves and a dust mask, wetting droppings first to reduce dust.
  • Reduce food: clean up spilled grain promptly.

Some birds are protected under provincial conservation laws. Check requirements before any trapping or lethal control and never use unregistered poisons.

Completing the service

  1. Record all treatments: pests, areas, products and registration numbers, quantities, stations serviced and monitor counts.
  2. Update the site plan and trend records.
  3. Give the client a service report with findings, treatments, precautions and required client actions.
  4. Clean equipment and secure waste for correct disposal.
  5. Schedule the next service or follow-up.

Key points

  • Use secured, numbered, labelled bait stations and traps rather than poison inside food areas.
  • Remove carcasses and get urgent medical or veterinary help if bait may have been eaten.
  • Treat cockroaches with gel baits in cracks near harbourages and never spray over baits.
  • Eliminate breeding sites for flies and mosquitoes and service light traps on schedule.
  • Manage birds mainly by exclusion and check protection status before other control.

quiz.question: Why are rodenticide blocks secured on rods inside bait stations?

options.text: To make them last longer in rain
So bait cannot be dragged out and spread

quiz.question: Where should cockroach gel bait be placed?

options.text: In small dots in cracks near harbourages
In large blobs in the middle of the floor

quiz.question: Where should an insect light trap be placed in a food area?

options.text: Facing the outside door so it can be seen from outside
Away from food lines and not visible from outside

quiz.question: What is the main approach to managing pest birds?

options.text: Exclusion with netting, spikes and closing holes

quiz.question: A child may have eaten rodent bait. What should be done?

options.text: Get medical help immediately with the product label
Nothing if the child seems fine
